findings: All nine native labels and 30 accepted forms have clear culinary senses. Egg parts stay distinct; powdered milk is not infant-formula ownership; starch and mixer keep qualified names. Existing plain mixer projection is preserved.

Edges 0–7: egg parts and variant-specific yolk/white preparation roles are explicitly supported by dictionary and original cozonac, amandina, crustless-pasca, cream and ice-cream recipes. No ingredient arrow is reversed.

Edges 8–16: powdered sugar milling/dusting/cream uses and milk dehydration are direct definitions or documented uses. Powdered milk is a variant chocolate/ice-cream ingredient and coffee addition, not a universal ingredient or nutrition claim.

Edges 17–31: suitable sweet cream, sugar, real vanilla, chilling and a mixer explain whipped cream; five familiar ingredients explain vanilla cream. Starch in eclair dough and ice cream is explicitly variant-qualified. Cream filling and dessert peer identities are not collapsed.

Edges 32–36: freezer/ice-cream storage is distinct from refrigeration; optional freezer compartments, frozen bread, qualified milk and strawberries have manufacturer/producer evidence. No storage temperatures/durations or quality guarantees are authored.
Edges 37–40: mixer labels describe beating/mixing with suitable attachments, not manufacturing egg whites or requiring a machine for every cozonac.

All 41 links are one-way, specific and nonduplicate. Nine concepts have at least four incident neighbors; only the two cream concepts have five incoming clues. Source-only concepts are not automatically hidden targets.
